'''Maria Petrou''' [[FREng]] ({{langx|el|Μαρία Πέτρου}}; 17 May 1953 – 15 October 2012)<ref name=Ob>{{cite news|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/obituaries/science-obituaries/9670656/Professor-Maria-Petrou.html|title=Professor Maria Petrou|work=[[The Daily Telegraph]]|date=11 November 2012|accessdate=12 November 2012}}</ref> was a [[Greece|Greek]]-born [[United Kingdom|British]] scientist who specialised in the fields of [[artificial intelligence]] and [[machine vision]]. She developed a number of novel [[image recognition]] techniques, taught at [[Surrey University]] and [[Imperial College London]], and was a prolific author of scientific articles.<ref name=Ob/>

==Early life and education==
Petrou was born in [[Thessaloniki]], Greece, in 1953, and displayed an aptitude for science from an early age.<ref name=Ob/> She began tutoring children in maths and science at the age of 15. She studied [[physics]] at the [[Aristotle University of Thessaloniki]], before travelling to the United Kingdom to study [[mathematics]] and [[astronomy]] at the [[University of Cambridge]].<ref name=ICL/> In 1983, Petrou began working as a postdoctoral research assistant at [[Oxford University]]'s Department of Theoretical Physics.<ref name=ICL/>

==Artificial intelligence research==
As British academia gained a more practical focus in the 1980s, Petrou began to study [[machine vision]] and other aspects of [[robot]]ic intelligence. In 1988, she started work at the [[University of Surrey]]'s Department of Electronic and Electrical Engineering, becoming its Professor of Image Analysis in 1998.<ref name=Ob/> She later held the Chair of Signal Processing at [[Imperial College London]], and was the Director of the Informatics and Telematics Institute at Greece's Centre for Research and Technology (CERTH) from 2009 until her death.<ref name=IAPR>{{cite web|url=http://www.iapr.org/news/index.php?id=531|title=In Memoriam – Dr. Maria Petrou|publisher=IAPR|date=16 October 2012|accessdate=12 November 2012}}</ref><ref name=ICL/> Petrou was furthermore elected a Fellow of the [[Royal Academy of Engineering]], authored several books, and was a prolific contributor to scientific journals.<ref name=Ob/>

During her career, Petrou developed a number of important image recognition techniques, including methods for robotic texture analysis, image comparison and 3D measurement.<ref name=Ob/> Most notably, she and Dr Alexander Kadyrov co-invented the trace transform,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www2.ee.ic.ac.uk/publications/p4673.pdf|title= The Trace transform and its applications|publisher=IEEE|year=2001}}</ref> a method of image representation that allows for more efficient [[facial recognition system]]s.<ref>{{cite book|chapter= A Trace transform based on subspace method for face recognition|publisher=IEEE Xplore|year=2010|doi= 10.1109/ICCASM.2010.5622706|isbn= 978-1-4244-7235-2|title= 2010 International Conference on Computer Application and System Modeling (ICCASM 2010)|last1= Zhan Shi|last2= Minghui Du|last3= Rongbing Huang|pages= V13-170-V13-172|s2cid=17374302}}</ref> Technologies based on Petrou's work have had numerous applications in commerce, medicine and environmental imaging.<ref name=Ob/> She was also an amateur [[cartoon]]ist, and once challenged her colleagues to construct a robot capable of [[ironing]] clothes – a challenge that later developed into a [[European Union]]-funded robotics project.<ref name=Ob/><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.clopema.eu/|title=CloPeMa|publisher=Clopema.eu|accessdate=12 November 2012}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Petrou married Phil L. Palmer, a British astronomer, with whom she had one son before divorcing.<ref name=Ob/> She died of [[cancer]] in October 2012, aged 59.<ref name=Ob/>
